content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Underestimates during prolonged downward trends; add 1–2% to forecast when 3+ consecutive days show falling prices.
- Overreacts to minor price volatility; smooth out forecast changes by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before predicting next day.
- Consistently underestimates true outcomes in the 10–15 day horizon; increase forecast by 2–4% for 10–15 day ahead predictions.
- Shows lag in response to policy or supply shocks; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days when major news or regulatory changes occur.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
